implementerProof.how: I drove the same surface independently: Dispatch built at ff684ac1 and at main 1f5b0828 on a Postgres 16.2 and a NATS of my own, and INFRA-589's harness (on main) for load. Verified: ordinary out-of-order commits, concurrency on one and two processes, the replay_complete rules carried to the socket, the reset waits, the fresh-process first start, the old lock, references since, the NATS order, whoami's final event_head, the bounded first start on 5,000,122 ids when no writer is open (events_start 38-44 ms), and 89 connections. Rejected on the architect's item 1. When a write in Dispatch's database holds its transaction id from before the boot mark into the first start, which is a restart under load, the bound falls back to reading every id from 0. It is logged ('reads every event id above the proven horizon'), and on 5M ids it costs seconds.

failures.criterion: Every consumer of the event stream keeps the order it relies on, at production size (INFRA-514's architect, this round: re-measure the bounded first start on 5M ids and check the bound with a writer whose transaction began before the mark; a read from id 0 or a wait of seconds is a failure).
failures.evidence: Red test c6e566654bab: TestTheRelaysFirstStartDoesNotReadTheWholeEventLogWhileAWriterFromBeforeBootIsOpen in packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/live_events_horizon_test.go. It opens a writer in the test's database before register takes the boot mark (through testServerOptions.persistence, which runs on the database before register), fills 200,000 events, subscribes cold, and releases the writer 1 s into the start, as a write holding its id for seconds does. It fails twice: 'the relay's first start read 200021 rows of events on a log of 200000 events while a writer from before the boot mark was open, want at most 20000'. It passes with a local edit I reverted, used only as its control: firstRelayFloor takes a fresh mark every 50 ms until WriterFloor accepts one. The start waits for that writer anyway (Horizon.Await), so waiting for a qualifying mark costs nothing extra. The same commit hardens my round-10 test: both now count events rows read by sequential scan as well as through events_pkey, after ending the other connections so their statistics are flushed. The old idx_tup_read count missed a full read that Postgres planned as a sequential scan, and missed statistics a pooled backend had not yet flushed. The round-10 test still passes at the head. Command: cd packages/envoy && DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres@127.0.0.1:16432/postgres?sslmode=disable go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run TestTheRelaysFirstStartDoesNotReadTheWholeEventLog -count=2 -v. Real surface, 5,000,122 ids, a newly started head process: (a) a psql write open since before boot and committed 2 s after the first cold subscription: full-read warning logged, events_start 2.96 s after that commit, its event and the next both delivered; (b) the same write opened after the boot mark: no warning, events_start 0.20 s after its commit; (c) four writers in Dispatch's database, each holding its id for 3 s and overlapping with no break, subscription 0.5 s after /healthz: full-read warning, events_start 6.01 s after subscribe; the same writers with the subscription 5 s and 10 s after /healthz: no warning, 3.12 s and 2.87 s, which is the horizon's own wait for those writers; (d) writers holding 1 s: no warning, 0.89 s. A deploy under load restarts the process while seconds-long write transactions are open, and pages resubscribe at once, so case (c) is a deploy's: about 3 s more per first subscription on 5M ids, linear in the log. The bound's ordering is safe in every case: every event committed after the start reached the first subscription, in id order.
